About Wheely

Wheely is redefining premium transportation across major cities in Europe, the US, and the Middle East. We blend cutting-edge technology with the craft of five-star chauffeuring to deliver an experience trusted by more than 100,000 active riders and 1,200 corporate accounts.

We’re a profitable, fast-growing scale-up with $43M raised and over $100M in annual revenue. Having recently launched in New York City, we’re expanding rapidly across the US and EMEA. If you take pride in your craft and want to help shape the next chapter of our growth, we'd love to hear from you.

About The Role

We’re looking for a Backend Engineer to join one of our teams that keeps frameworks lean and focuses on what matters: clean, maintainable code, shipped fast with TDD, DDD, and continuous integration and delivery.

We are a Go shop, and while we’re busy migrating away from our Ruby monolith, our stack includes PostgreSQL, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Redis, gRPC, and Thrift. Everything runs on AWS and Kubernetes, managed via Terraform.

Our interview process includes a recruiter screen, algorithms and live coding. Senior+ candidates also complete a system design section and a structured review of past experience and achievements.

Responsibilities

  • Write high-quality, performant code primarily in Go.
  • Implement new microservices while helping us responsibly manage and migrate away from legacy services.
  • Work closely with product managers, designers, and data scientists to turn abstract requirements into concrete technical designs.
  • Ensure our systems stay responsive under heavy load, optimising for both latency and reliability.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience building and maintaining scalable backend services.
  • We use Go. If you know it, great. If not, we’ll interview you in your strongest language (Python, C++, Ruby, etc.). We hire for engineering fundamentals, not syntax.
  • In-depth knowledge of relational and NoSQL databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis) and experience with message brokers like RabbitMQ or Kafka.
  • Upper-Intermediate (B2) English proficiency or higher. You should be comfortable debating technical trade-offs with your peers.

What We Offer

What We Offer

  • Office-based role in West London, four days a week with flexible start and finish times, plus one remote day of your choice
  • Salary starting from £90,000
  • Employee stock options plan
  • Private medical and dental insurance
  • Life and critical illness cover
  • Latest-generation MacBook Pro and 4k display
  • Monthly credit towards Wheely journeys
  • Cycle to Work scheme
  • Professional development stipend
  • Relocation support, including visa sponsorship and allowance

All of your personal information will be collected stored and processed in accordance with Wheely’s Candidate Privacy Notice

description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Position Summary

The Campaign Lead is a senior role within the Market Development Capability Area, responsible for owning and driving complex customer opportunities from early shaping through to contract award. You will develop and lead the campaign strategy, bringing together expertise from across Metrea to understand customer requirements, develop differentiated solutions and position the business to win.  

The primary focus will be on campaigns in manned airborne ISR, Air Transport and Aerial Fire Fighting, with the potential to integrate Metrea’s Electromagnetic & Cyber and Digital & Synthetic capabilities into solutions. You will have a deep understanding of Air domain effects, sensors and capabilities, the missions they are employed within and the markets and customers that require them. Based from our London office with hybrid working, you will be responsible for developing and delivering winning campaigns from early shaping and campaign planning through bid submission, contract award and transition to delivery, supporting national security customers including the UK Ministry of Defence, NATO and allied partners.  

You will work closely with Market Development leads and teams across Metrea, bringing together the operational, technical, commercial and delivery expertise required to develop and execute successful campaign strategies across the EMEA region. Working closely with the Bids & Proposals team, you will provide strategic and content leadership for complex bids and proposals. You will develop the win strategy, value proposition and key messages, translate technical and operational inputs into compelling customer-focused content and ensure the campaign strategy is consistently reflected through the proposal.  You will be trained in the Metrea Solution Framework and, after contract award, will work with Programme Leads to ensure the customer need is delivered and to identify opportunities to grow our services.

What You'll Do

  • Lead campaign activity from early customer engagement and opportunity shaping through solution development, bid generation and contract award
  • Lead customer, market and competitive analysis, including stakeholder mapping, customer needs, procurement intelligence and competitor positioning, to inform the campaign strategy
  • Develop and execute customer and stakeholder engagement plans to shape opportunities, influence requirements and position Metrea effectively, building strong relationships across Defence and the EMEA region
  • Work with Solution Architects and SMEs to translate customer requirements and solution design outputs into a differentiated, deliverable proposition
  • Develop the teaming approach and identify and coordinate strategic partnerships required to strengthen the campaign and solution
  • Develop the win strategy, value proposition, win themes and key messages that differentiate Metrea and provide a clear basis for the proposal
  • Own the proposal strategy and develop compelling, customer-focused content, including executive level messaging, by translating technical, operational and commercial inputs into a clear and coherent narrative
  • Provide clear content direction to SMEs, Finance, Legal, Operations and other contributors, ensuring the win strategy and key messages are consistently reflected throughout the proposal
  • Lead price-to-win development, working with Finance and other relevant stakeholders to align the commercial approach with the campaign strategy and competitive environment
  • Present and defend campaign strategies and recommendations through internal reviews and approval processes, responding effectively to challenges from senior stakeholders

What You Bring

  • Significant experience leading complex campaigns or customer opportunities within the Aerospace and Defence sector, with demonstratable ownership from early opportunity shaping through bid and contract award
  • Strong understanding of Air domain missions, with particular emphasis is on manned airborne ISR. Experience across additional Air domain mission sets, such as Aerial Fire Fighting, Air to Air Refueling, or Strategic Transport and Mobility, is desirable
  • Demonstratable experienced leading the strategy and content development for complex Aerospace and Defence bids and proposals, including coordinating multidisciplinary inputs
  • Strong understanding of the Aerospace and Defence market in the EMEA region, with experience of customer engagement, opportunity shaping and working with senior customers and industry stakeholders
  • Strong strategic and analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex customer, market and competitive information and translate it into clear and actionable campaign strategy
  • Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical, operational and commercial information into clear, persuasive and customer-focused proposal content
  • Experience developing executive-level messaging, value propositions and win themes for complex customer proposals
  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with the confidence and credibility to present, challenge and defend recommendations with senior internal and external stakeholders

Benefits

  • Private Medical Insurance  
  • Subsided gym membership / plans through Wellhub  
  • Electric Car scheme  
  • Cycle to work scheme  
  • Salary sacrificed pension scheme  
  • Free lunch on office days  
  • Enhanced Parental Leave  
  • 30 days annual PTO plus b/h 
  • Bonus Scheme 
  • Personal development opportunities

Work Authorization / Security Clearance

The employee will have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom and will be able to produce right to work documentation. Ability to achieve full UK SC and DV is essential. 

AAP/EEO Statement

Metrea Management Limited (MAME) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or other characteristics protected by law. 

Position Type and Expected Hours of Work

This is a full-time position of 40 hours per week with typical working hours of Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Hours and work shifts may change in accordance with department and business needs. Employees in this role may be required to work over 40 hours per week with approval from the department manager.

Work Environment

Office environment, 3 days a week at our Hammersmith office. 

Travel

Regular travel is required to support campaigns, customer engagement and industry events across the EMEA region, with occasional travel elsewhere for workshops and other Enterprise activities. 

Our Firmware

At Metrea, our single core value is Rooted in Humility, and our four cornerstone attributes are Entrepreneurial, Systematic, Discerning, and Over-Deliver. These form what we call our Teammate Firmware. Just like technical firmware connects software and hardware, our Firmware is the constant interface between our mission and our people. It defines how we show up, how we work together, and how we solve complex problems.

Our team Firmware creates a web-like, hyper-collaborative, dynamically hierarchical way of working that helps us adapt quickly, communicate openly, and distribute decision-making to where expertise actually lives. It enables groups to self-organize around hard problems, shift fluidly as priorities evolve, and operate with the trust, curiosity, and discipline required in a complex mission space. This foundation allows us to deliver elegant, effective solutions and uphold our purpose: protecting our precious inheritance.

description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. Amsterdam or London | Reports to Senior Director, Product The opportunity Checkout.com helps businesses thrive in the digital economy by making payments work better. Fraud is central to that mission: we need to protect our merchants and Checkout without blocking good customers or adding unnecessary friction. We are looking for a Group Product Manager to lead the fraud domain across Payment Performance. You will own the strategy for building our fraud engine with real-time models, controls and decisioning capabilities that protect Checkout and the products built on top of it. The ambition is to build a best-in-class fraud platform: one that performs at the highest level, adapts as fraud changes and works equally well for merchants as it does to protect Checkout. Protecting Checkout from fraud has significant value for the overall payment performance, This is a portfolio leadership role. You will lead several Product Managers, co-own the Fraud Data Science roadmap and work closely with Engineering, Analytics, Fraud Operations and Design. You will also spend time with some of the world’s most sophisticated merchants to understand their fraud challenges, prove value and shape what we build next. What you’ll do Set the fraud strategy Create one product vision and roadmap across merchant fraud products, real-time decisioning and Checkout-wide protection. Decide where we need to close core gaps and where we can build differentiated capabilities that change the basis of competition. Balance merchant fraud, Checkout losses, acceptance impact, FDP revenue and operational effort when setting priorities. Define how our fraud capabilities should support Enterprise merchants, Platforms, SMBs and other Checkout products as their needs evolve. Build a best-in-class fraud platform Improve the performance, coverage and resilience of our real-time fraud decisioning. Build products that let merchants choose the right level of control: configure their own protection, act on intelligent recommendations or delegate decisions to Autopilot. Build a platform that enables our internal teams to investigate and respond to fraud trends and fraud attacks, then turn this into better protection for Checkout and our merchants Strengthen how merchants monitor, explain and improve fraud decisions through better controls, recommendations, alerting and investigation experiences. Expand protection against new fraud types using better data, specialized models and faster learning loops. Shape Product and Data Science together Co-own the Fraud Data Science roadmap and outcome metrics with the Data Science leader. Ensure Product chooses the right problems, customer outcomes and trade-offs while Data Science owns methods, model quality and scientific rigor. Connect model performance and platform investment to visible merchant and business outcomes. Build the feedback loops between models, merchant products, analytics and operations that allow our protection to keep improving. Guide investment toward capabilities that improve fraud performance at scale, not technical progress in isolation. Grow the portfolio and its value Own the product economics of the fraud portfolio, including value measurement, investment cases, adoption strategy and input into packaging and pricing. Partner with teams across Checkout include Commercial and Product Marketing to turn complex fraud capabilities into a clear merchant proposition. Build credible ways to demonstrate the value of our fraud products before and after launch. Work with Risk Operations to define clear boundaries, handovers and feedback loops between automated transaction decisions and account-level operations. Lead the team Lead, coach and develop Product Managers across the fraud portfolio. Give teams clear ownership, goals and decision rights while building a strong shared purpose. Create an effective operating model across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, Design and Fraud Operations. Align senior stakeholders around evidence-based priorities, investment choices and trade-offs. What success looks like In your first 12–18 months, you will have: United FDP, Autopilot, core fraud decisioning and Checkout protection behind one strategy, metric framework and roadmap. Improved measurable fraud performance while managing the impact on acceptance, Checkout losses and operational effort. Closed priority product gaps and made the merchant fraud experience more competitive and coherent. Established a stronger joint operating model across Product, Data Science, Engineering and Fraud Operations. Built a high-performing team of Product Managers with clear accountability across the fraud domain. What we’re looking for Essential Deep experience building fraud or risk products in payments, fintech, commerce or another high-volume decisioning environment. Strong understanding of fraud models, rules, controls and the trade-offs between fraud prevention, false positives and customer experience. A track record of setting strategy and delivering outcomes across multiple related products or teams. Proven success leading and developing Product Managers. The ability to bring clarity and structure to complex, ambiguous problem spaces. Strong quantitative judgment and experience using model performance, experimentation and financial analysis to make decisions. Credibility with Engineering and Data Science teams building real-time, ML-powered products. Commercial judgment and the ability to connect technical capabilities to customer value, adoption and sustainable business outcomes. Clear, persuasive communication with merchants, teams and senior executives. We care more about the scope of the problems you have solved and the outcomes you have delivered than a fixed number of years in a particular title. Valuable, but not required Experience building adaptive or automated fraud products such as dynamic strategies or recommendations. Knowledge of fraud operations, investigations, disputes and the handoffs between automated and human decisions. Experience supporting multiple merchant segments, platforms or embedded payment products. Experience shaping packaging, pricing or value-based commercial models for fraud products. How we work This role is based in Amsterdam or London and follows Checkout.com’s hybrid working model. You will report to the Senior Director, Product and work across Product, Technology, Data, Risk and Commercial within the Payment Performance pillar. Additional Information Bring all of you to work We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection. Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us. How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. 🔍 The Interview Process: Our process is clear and respectful of your time: Initial call / recruiter screen Competency Interviews Deep-dive interviews Final interview: mission & values alignment We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability. description: At Scality, we build software that stores and protects the world’s most critical data — running on Linux, inside some of the largest infrastructures on the planet, at exabyte scale, for organizations that cannot afford to fail. We are looking for a Platform Security Engineer to join our platform and delivery team in Paris. This is a new seat, and it exists because security work needs dedicated capacity. Absorbed as background tasks between feature tickets, it never gets the focus it deserves. You would be that dedicated capacity. This is a Linux-first, hands-on engineering role. You will not write policies for other people to implement — you will write the Python and Bash that hardens our OS, automates our vulnerability management, and proves to auditors and customers that our supply chain is sound. About Scality Scality is the leader in software-defined object storage, trusted by 1,000+ enterprises and 700M+ users worldwide across banking, healthcare, and government sectors — exactly the sectors where security posture is a purchasing criterion, not a checkbox. Industry recognition: Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for 9 consecutive years — the only 100% software-defined storage company to hold this position since the quadrant’s inception #1 on the GigaOm Radar for Enterprise Object Storage (2024), ahead of 17 competing vendors Gold Stevie Award 2025 — ARTESCA 3.0, Cloud Storage & Backup Solution category Net Promoter Score of 85 across RING and ARTESCA About the team You will join a small team of highly skilled Linux engineers responsible for delivering and maintaining ADI (Scality Autonomous Data Infrastructure), our full platform: RING (object storage), S3C (S3-compatible layer), and SCOS (Scality OS — our own Linux distribution). The team works across the full stack of infrastructure engineering — deep Linux system integration, RPM packaging, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and release automation. The command line is where most of our day happens, and we ship a Linux distribution to customers. How We Build We build with AI tools, in earnest rather than as an experiment. Every engineer here has Claude Code, and it is part of how we write, review, and ship code day to day. We are also designing something larger: an AI code and delivery factory — AI woven into the build and release chain itself, not just into the editor. That work is early and still being thought through rather than already solved. We expect it to become part of how we maintain the platform, and CVE remediation is one of the first places we think it fits: an automated path from advisory to assessment to a patched, tested, delivered build. If that sounds like a problem you would want to work on, this role sits close to it. One principle is not negotiable: a human owns the outcome. AI writes code here, and when it does, we own what it produces — the review, the decision to ship, the consequences, and the fix. “The tool did it” is not an explanation we accept from ourselves, and it is not one we would offer a customer. In security work that matters doubly: an answer you cannot defend is worse than no answer at all. How This Role Works Scality is building a network of security engineers across the engineering department — a security peer embedded in each development team, rather than a central security function working at arm’s length from the code. You would be that peer for the platform and delivery team. Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering. The agenda is set at that level, with dedicated resources committed across the teams. You will not have to invent it alone — and you will have a voice in it: the engineers closest to the code help decide what goes on the roadmap. We will be straight with you: today security work competes with delivery commitments and too often loses. Naming an owner and funding dedicated people is how we intend to change that. You would help build that capability, not inherit a finished one. The team is accountable for the deliveries. Security items sit on the team’s plate alongside everything else it commits to, rather than in a separate function filing tickets from the outside. You are the dedicated resource that makes them happen. While your teammates carry releases, OS compatibility, and platform features, your time is reserved for the security work. That focus is the whole reason the seat exists. You share the team’s perimeter and its knowledge. Same repositories, same Jira projects, same code reviews, same sprint rituals. The engineers around you have rare, hard-earned Linux depth — OS integration, RPM packaging, boot and GRUB, CI/CD, monitoring — and you will learn the platform from them. You will have peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams work the same problems on different perimeters. That network is where you compare notes, share tooling, and grow into the craft. The point of the model is that security decisions get made inside the team that builds and ships the product, by someone who understands the build system rather than filing tickets against it. Your First Missions Two priorities are already on the roadmap, and they will shape your first year. 1. CVE exposure, answered before it is asked Customers in banking, healthcare, and government ask us, routinely and under their own audit obligations, whether our products are exposed to a given CVE. That will not stop — for them, asking is the compliance requirement. Today each answer is researched from scratch: a customer question becomes a ticket, the ticket becomes a hunt through SBOMs, vendor advisories, and our own configuration, and the round trip can take weeks to produce something the team is not fully confident defending. Your first mission is to invert that, so the answer already exists when the question arrives. A standing exposure record, per shipped component and per release: what the SBOM says is present, what the upstream vendor has decided (including “will not fix”, which is common on RHEL 8 and often the real answer), and whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable in our configuration Reachability over presence. A module shipped and loaded by a distribution default is not the same as a module configured on a live URL. That distinction is the difference between “vulnerable” and “no impact”, and it is where the engineering judgement lives Continuous CVE detection across our repositories, vendored third-party modules, container images, and shipped RPMs Wiring detection into our existing SBOM tooling and GitHub Actions pipelines, so exposure is computed when a release is built rather than when a customer asks A defined interface with the security engineers and the customer-facing teams: who produces the technical assessment, who owns the wording that reaches the customer, and how both meet the response commitments in our customer security policy Durable capture. An assessment that lives only in a ticket comment gets re-derived next release. Findings belong somewhere queryable A remediation loop with clear ownership and response targets, integrated with how the team already works in Jira AI-assisted remediation, where it fits: from advisory to proposed patch to a tested build, with a human deciding what ships Done well, a customer’s “are you affected by X?” becomes a lookup and an afternoon, not an escalation and three weeks. 2. Raising the security baseline of SCOS SCOS is our own Linux distribution — we control the kickstarts, the package set, the boot path, and the images. That is unusual leverage, and we intend to use it. You will drive platform-level hardening across the OS we ship: A hardened, defensible default configuration for the distribution Advancing SELinux enforcement across RING and S3C (work already begun on the team, which you will help carry) Supply-chain integrity: artifact provenance, signing, dependency currency, reproducible and verifiable builds Secrets and credential handling across the delivery pipeline Cryptographic posture — including FIPS 140-3 readiness, which matters concretely: FIPS 140-2 certificates move to NIST’s historical list on 22 September 2026, and RHEL 9’s validated OpenSSL, GnuTLS, and kernel crypto modules are the foundation we build on Compliance-driven engineering work, notably the supply-chain security expectations of NIS2 (Article 21(2)(d)) and the EU Cyber Resilience Act — translated into automation and evidence, not spreadsheets You will also contribute to what comes next: threat modelling of the platform, hardening guidance for customers, and security review of significant design changes. What We Are Looking For This is a role for someone early in their career who wants to grow into being their team’s security reference. We expect to invest in you, and we expect you to keep growing here for as long as you want to — there is no ceiling built into this seat. Required Linux is your primary operating system — at work, at home, or both. You are comfortable in the terminal and you reach for a shell before a UI Roughly 2–4 years of relevant experience, or a shorter track record with unusually strong evidence of the skills below Solid working ability in Python and Bash — you will be writing and maintaining real code in a production codebase A genuine, demonstrable interest in security. We care much more about this than about formal credentials. Show it however it is true for you: CTFs, a home lab, reading advisories and CVE writeups for fun, a hardening project, security-adjacent contributions, a blog, anything real Comfortable using Git in a collaborative environment Ability to read and understand existing code before modifying it The judgement to tell a real risk from a scanner’s opinion — and the instinct to check whether vulnerable code is actually reachable before calling it exposed The willingness to say plainly when you are not yet sure, rather than producing an answer you could not defend French — the team works in French day to day Written communication skills in English Nice to Have CVE triage, CVSS scoring, or vulnerability management experience Reading vendor advisories and understanding vendor triage — NVD, RHSA, Red Hat severity and will-not-fix calls Supply-chain security tooling — SBOM formats (SPDX, CycloneDX), scanners (Trivy, Grype, Syft), artifact signing RPM packaging or Linux distribution internals SELinux policy work CI/CD systems, especially GitHub Actions RHEL / Rocky Linux (versions 8 and 9) Containers (Docker, containerd, systemd units) Ansible or Salt Awareness of NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, or FIPS 140-3 Familiarity with S3 or object storage concepts Serious use of AI coding tools in a real workflow — Claude Code or equivalent, beyond autocomplete To Be Clear About Scope This is a software engineering role with a security mandate. It is not a SOC or incident-response analyst position, not a penetration-testing role, and not a GRC or compliance-documentation role. If what you want is to build the tooling and harden the system yourself, in code, you are in the right place. What We Offer Dedicated focus. Security is your job here, not the thing you get to after the sprint work is done Clear direction, and a say in it. Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering, and the team is accountable for delivering them. You would not be inventing the agenda on your own, you would help shape what goes on it, and you would be part of making it stick A network of peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams, working the same problems on different perimeters Work that compounds. Customer security questions are a permanent obligation, so every assessment you make reusable and every check you automate keeps paying back, release after release Modern tooling, actually adopted. Claude Code in every engineer’s hands, and a real say in how AI reshapes our build and delivery chain A rare combination: security work with the leverage of owning the whole stack, down to our own Linux distribution Mentorship from senior engineers with deep expertise across Linux, storage, packaging, and distributed systems — you will not be the only person who understands your perimeter A long-term growth path toward becoming your team’s security reference and a senior voice in the network Work that ships to production and runs at exabyte scale, in banking, healthcare, and government Standard French benefits: meal vouchers, Navigo subsidy, mutuelle Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

Principal Analyst II, Revenue Operations

The Revenue Strategy & Operations team ensures that our global sales/revenue organization is positioned to achieve their highest potential by optimizing revenue opportunities across the globe. Qualtrics is seeking a Field Operations Partner to support our EMEA Sales Teams, responsible for setting new business and renewal targets, optimizing territories to ensure the greatest opportunity for each individual rep's success, and leading other key strategic revenue-enhancing initiatives.

What You Should Know About This Team

  • Fun, inviting, and inclusive team made up of passionate, kind, and smart people who exemplify what it means to be Customer Obsessed

Automation & Software Engineering

description: Il y a vingt ans, les premières sélections Les Composantes voyaient le jour. Une histoire née d’une soif d’indépendance et d’une passion pour le vintage. Une manière instinctive de faire circuler les vêtements, guidée par une attention particulière à ce qui dure. Dans son prolongement, Sézane prend vie en 2013 : la première marque de mode française née en ligne. Puis sont venus enrichir cet univers : Octobre Éditions pour les hommes, Les Composantes, dédiée cette fois à l’art de vivre, et Petit Sézane pour les enfants. Tout s’est construit comme on avance dans la vie : par élans, par gestes spontanés avec cette manière d’apprendre en faisant. Une autre relation au détail, au service et au lien. Une autre manière d’habiller le réel, d’abord en ligne, puis à travers nos Appartements. Nous recherchons aujourd’hui des talents créatifs, structurés et agiles qui partagent l’envie d’améliorer sans cesse tout ce qui peut l’être. Des talents passionnés, autonomes qui conçoivent le travail dans le respect des autres et pour qui rien n'est hors d'atteinte, pour peu qu'on s'en donne les moyens. Rattaché(e) à la direction d'Octobre Éditions, le/la Responsable Marketing (H/F) définit et pilote la stratégie marketing de la marque. Du lancement 360° des collections à l'animation de la communauté et des points de vente, en passant par les contenus, le CRM et les collaborations, le/la Responsable Marketing développe la désirabilité d’Octobre et contribue à sa croissance. Ce poste est basé à Paris (75). Vos principales responsabilités seront : 1. Stratégie marketing et pilotage de la marque Établir et piloter la stratégie marketing globale d'Octobre Élaborer les stratégies de lancement 360° des collections, en lien avec les différentes équipes de la marque Construire le calendrier commercial en coordination avec les équipes concernées 2. Paid media et contenus Piloter la stratégie paid en lien avec les équipes dédiées Concevoir les contenus éditoriaux sur l'ensemble des supports (newsletters, réseaux sociaux, campagnes paid media, site, application) en France et à l'international Accompagner la stratégie de la marque sur les réseaux sociaux 3. Expérience client et CRM Définir la stratégie d'expérience client omnicanale Concevoir les initiatives dédiées à l'engagement des meilleurs clients (parcours CRM et transactionnels) 4. Animation commerciale et événementielle Suivre et analyser les opérations commerciales et marketing Imaginer, coordonner et déployer les animations commerciales et événementielles lors des temps forts de la marque, dans les points de vente existants et futurs 5. Collaborations Identifier les opportunités de collaboration dans le cadre de la stratégie de développement de la marque Assurer la gestion opérationnelle des collaborations en coordination avec les équipes concernées 6. Coordination et management Coordonner et synchroniser les prises de parole avec les équipes Sézane Accompagner et suivre les équipes de manière hebdomadaire Requirements Vous avez entre 8 et 10 ans d'expérience en marketing ou en branding, dans une marque de mode ou une plateforme e-commerce, idéalement avec une identité forte. Vous maîtrisez le marketing 360° (social, CRM, paid, événementiel, retail) et vous aimez passer de l'idée à l'exécution. Vous avez une vraie sensibilité marque : vous savez raconter des histoires, créer la surprise et porter un univers créatif. Vous savez allier désirabilité de marque et performance commerciale, et vous suivez vos résultats pour ajuster vos actions. Vous savez coordonner plusieurs équipes et interlocuteurs, et vous avez une première expérience en management d’équipe. Vous êtes force de proposition, autonome et organisé(e), et vous aimez construire dans un environnement agile en développement. Vous souhaitez évoluer dans un environnement international et disposez pour cela d’un Anglais courant. Octobre recrute et valorise tous les talents, quels que soient votre genre, âge, nationalité, culture, croyances religieuses et orientations sexuelles. description: About Airwallex Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own. We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full. About the Team The Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) team at Airwallex is a strategically vital function operating under a clear Three Lines of Defence model. As the independent second line, FCC owns the global AML/CTF programme, sanctions framework, risk assessment methodology, and governance infrastructure across all global entities. As Airwallex scales into new markets and deepens its engagement with global regulatory bodies, we are building a world-class compliance organization capable of managing complex financial crime risks at scale. This is an environment where you will tackle high-impact challenges, shape global fintech risk strategies, and help establish foundations for long-term growth. What you'll do As Senior Associate, FCC Monitoring & Testing, EMEA you will shape and scale Airwallex’s global financial crime compliance monitoring and testing framework, establishing a rigorous, data-driven second-line assurance function. You will independently validate the design and operating effectiveness of AML, Sanctions, and KYC/KYB controls across all production environments and establish a monitoring framework and associated metrics to support executive decisioning and ongoing maintenance of program and control operating effectiveness. You will work closely with the broader FCC organization, Product, Engineering, Operations, and regional leadership to turn testing insights into operational accountability, robust remediation, and a defensible compliance posture before global regulators and institutional banking partners. This role covers the EMEA region and is based remotely in Birmingham. In this role, you will be a key part of a global team, collaborating closely across regions to drive consistent FCC Monitoring & Testing standards. Responsibilities: Contribute to the strategic development, execution, and continuous evolution of Airwallex’s Global FCC Monitoring & Testing Programme, establishing robust, risk-based testing methodologies and annual plans for independent second-line assurance. Design comprehensive testing frameworks to validate core compliance controls across customer onboarding, periodic reviews, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, and regulatory reporting workflows, ensuring coverage keeps pace with product and market expansion. Oversee the ongoing FCC monitoring program for EMEA, including establishment of KPIs and operating effectiveness metrics. Advance the transition from traditional sample reviews toward continuous, data-enabled assurance by leveraging data analytics, system logs, and automated testing scripts to evaluate compliance control performance at the population level. Oversee the independent validation of system-encoded controls, including transaction monitoring thresholds, screening logic, and customer risk-rating models, ensuring systems function as intended without logic drift or hidden control gaps. Translate complex testing outcomes and thematic trends into clear, decision-useful reporting for executive leadership and governance forums, providing constructive challenge to stakeholders and tracking the root-cause remediation of control deficiencies. Represent the FCC monitoring and testing function during regulatory examinations, internal or external audits, and banking partner reviews, confidently defending testing methodologies and control evidence. Who you are We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory. Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Law, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related quantitative/analytical discipline. CAMS certification or an ICA International Diploma in Governance, Risk, and Compliance (or equivalent professional credential). 7+ years of experience within FCC quality assurance, compliance monitoring, internal audit, or a related second/third-line control function inside a fintech, payments, or highly regulated banking environment. Strong technical knowledge of financial crime controls across transaction monitoring, sanctions/PEP screening, customer due diligence, and digital KYC/KYB workflows. Proven mastery of risk-based testing methodologies, including scoping, sampling, design and operating effectiveness assessments, issue writing, and remediation validation. A high-ownership, pragmatic approach, with excellent written communication and stakeholder management skills to challenge senior partners constructively and drive operational accountability. Preferred qualifications: Advanced degree such as an MBA, Master’s in Regulatory Compliance, Risk Management, or a related field. Professional assurance or audit certifications such as CAMS-Audit, CISA, or CIA. Strong fintech and platforms experience, including exposure to cloud-native, API-driven, high-growth global environments with significant cross-border transaction volume. Strong data literacy, including comfort using SQL, Python, BI dashboards, or automated tools to support continuous control validation and population-based testing. Experience partnering directly with Product, Data Science, and Engineering teams to validate automated rules, model-driven controls, and rapid deployments within an agile product lifecycle. description:
About Wheely

Wheely is redefining premium transportation across major cities in Europe, the US, and the Middle East. We blend cutting-edge technology with the craft of five-star chauffeuring to deliver an experience trusted by more than 100,000 active riders and 1,200 corporate accounts.

We’re a profitable, fast-growing scale-up with $43M raised and over $100M in annual revenue. Having recently launched in New York City, we’re expanding rapidly across the US and EMEA. If you take pride in your craft and want to help shape the next chapter of our growth, we'd love to hear from you.

About The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join one of our teams that keeps frameworks lean and focuses on what matters: clean, maintainable code, shipped fast with TDD, DDD, and continuous integration and delivery.

We are a Go shop, and while we’re busy migrating away from our Ruby monolith, our stack includes PostgreSQL, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Redis, gRPC, and Thrift. Everything runs on AWS and Kubernetes, managed via Terraform.

Our interview process includes a recruiter screen, algorithms, live coding, a system design section, and a structured review of past experience and achievements.

Responsibilities

  • Write high-quality, performant code primarily in Go.
  • Implement new microservices while helping us responsibly manage and migrate away from legacy services.
  • Work closely with product managers, designers, and data scientists to turn abstract requirements into concrete technical designs.
  • Ensure our systems stay responsive under heavy load, optimising for both latency and reliability.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of experience building and maintaining scalable backend services.
  • We use Go. If you know it, great. If not, we’ll interview you in your strongest language (Python, C++, Ruby, etc.). We hire for engineering fundamentals, not syntax.
  • In-depth knowledge of relational and NoSQL databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis) and experience with message brokers like RabbitMQ or Kafka.
  • Upper-Intermediate (B2) English proficiency or higher. You should be comfortable debating technical trade-offs with your peers.

What We Offer

  • Office-based role in West London, four days a week with flexible start and finish times, plus one remote day of your choice
  • Salary starting from £120,000
  • Employee stock options plan
  • Private medical and dental insurance
  • Life and critical illness cover
  • Latest-generation MacBook Pro and 4k display
  • Monthly credit towards Wheely journeys
  • Cycle to Work scheme
  • Professional development stipend
  • Relocation support, including visa sponsorship and allowance

All of your personal information will be collected stored and processed in accordance with Wheely’s Candidate Privacy Notice

description: Build a Safer World. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. TRM Labs is hiring a Senior Capture Manager (UK) to support our most complex, high-impact deals, with an initial focus on public sector opportunities. This is not a traditional proposal writer or reactive Deal Desk role. The Senior Capture Manager will operate upstream in the sales cycle, partnering closely with Sales, Product, Legal, Security, and RevOps to shape deal strategy, influence decision criteria, and improve win probability before formal procurement begins. This role exists to increase quality, speed, and consistency across complex deals — while reducing risk, rework, and late-stage friction. What You’ll Do Capture & Deal Strategy Own capture strategy for PubSec opportunities globally and strategic public sector deals Engage early in the sales cycle (pre-RFP where possible) to: Shape requirements and evaluation criteria Influence Statements of Work and procurement language Align pricing, scope, and structure with long-term deal success Act as a strategic advisor to AEs on deal positioning, ROMs, and proposal framing Proposal Quality & Risk Management Lead capture execution for complex opportunities: Translate customer intent into compliant, outcome-driven proposals Ensure responses accurately reflect customer needs, constraints, and procurement realities Reduce late-stage surprises by identifying risk early and guiding teams through mitigation strategies Cross-Functional Orchestration Serve as a central point of coordination across: Sales Product & Engineering Legal Security & IT Finance & RevOps Triage what requires escalation vs. what can be resolved within Deal Desk Ensure the right teams are engaged at the right time — no earlier, no later Enablement & Continuous Improvement Build reusable capture templates, artifacts, and best practices Codify learnings from wins and losses to improve future deal execution Become a subject-matter expert in how TRM wins public sector deals What Success in the Role Looks Like Deals are shaped earlier, not rescued later Proposals reflect buyer intent, outcomes, and procurement realities Sales experiences faster momentum and fewer blockers Proposal quality improves without sacrificing speed Win rates increase for complex public sector opportunities Qualifications 5–10+ years experience in capture, deal strategy, or complex enterprise/public sector sales support Proven experience influencing outcomes before RFPs are finalized Background supporting complex, bespoke software or data platforms Strong written and verbal communication skills Ability to operate calmly across multiple high-stakes, concurrent deals About the Team: The RevOps team is truly remote! We practice async communication and collaboration through various methods such as slack channels and documentation (Notion, etc.). It's important to note that the primary method for communication for this role with all relevant stakeholders will be through slack (text, voice notes and video messages across DMs and various channels). Additionally, RevOps is involved in a variety of live recurring meetings throughout the week (~8 hours). A few times a year we'll come together in-person to collaborate, with an opportunity to engage in-person more often if you're near a hub. TRM Speed BI & Reporting Infrastructure: Built and deployed a fully automated BI dashboard in Looker within one week, reducing GTM reporting time by 60% and enabling real-time insights for leadership. Tech Stack & Automation: Optimized Salesforce workflows and integrated CPQ automation in under 48 hours, eliminating manual data entry and accelerating deal approvals by 3x. Revenue Planning & Strategy: Led a full-scale territory realignment in just three days, ensuring seamless execution and zero downtime for the sales team while improving coverage efficiency. Application Instructions If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team. Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role. If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered. Interviewing with TRM Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview. Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role. Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact. First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role. Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM. References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact. Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details. Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you! Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way. AI Fluency at TRM AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM. We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks. At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to: Accelerate repeatable workflows Structure and solve problems Improve output quality Increase speed and leverage You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process. Life at TRM We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day. TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days. Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving. At TRM, you should expect: Priorities and targets to change quickly Operating with a high degree of ambiguity A high level of personal ownership and accountability Close collaboration across teams and functions Frequent, high-touch communication Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment. We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Leadership Principles We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions. Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly. Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday. Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger. Join our Mission At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast. TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore. The Director of LV/Fiber Deployment leads the planning, execution, and operational handoff of low-voltage and fiber infrastructure deployments across data center, edge, and network facilities. This leader ensures deployments are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and to defined quality and reliability standards.

The role owns the end-to-end deployment lifecycle: design coordination, vendor strategy, material readiness, field execution, commissioning support, documentation, and turnover to operations.

  • Lead regional or global deployment programs for structured cabling, fiber backbone, low-voltage systems, and related physical infrastructure.
  • Build and lead a high-performing team of deployment managers, program managers, field engineers, and vendor partners.
  • Own deployment planning, schedules, resource models, budgets, forecasts, and executive reporting.
  • Partner with design, construction, network engineering, data center operations, supply chain, security, and commissioning teams to deliver production-ready infrastructure.
  • Establish standardized deployment playbooks, quality controls, acceptance criteria, and turnover processes.
  • Manage installation partners and vendors, including selection, performance management, capacity planning, safety, quality, and commercial accountability.
  • Drive deployment readiness by ensuring materials, labor, site access, permits, test equipment, and documentation are available ahead of execution.
  • Oversee fiber testing, labeling, documentation, as-built records, cable management, and remediation of quality issues.
  • Lead complex retrofits and live-site deployments while protecting customer availability, safety, and operational continuity.
  • Define and improve deployment KPIs, including on-time delivery, first-pass quality, cost per deployment, defect rates, safety performance, and time-to-service.
  • Identify deployment risks early, remove execution blockers, and lead escalation paths across internal and external stakeholders.

  • 5+ years leading multi-site teams, contractors, vendors, or complex deployment programs.
  • Deep knowledge of structured cabling, fiber-optic infrastructure, low-voltage systems, testing and certification practices, and cable-management standards.
  • Experience delivering infrastructure in data centers, telecom networks, industrial facilities, or other mission-critical environments.
  • Demonstrated success managing large vendor workforces, budgets, schedules, and quality programs.
  • Strong understanding of construction, commissioning, change control, site readiness, and operational handoff.
  • Proven ability to lead safely in live production environments and balance speed, quality, cost, and availability.
  • Excellent executive communication, cross-functional leadership, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

  • Experience supporting hyperscale cloud, AI/GPU infrastructure, or high-density data center deployments.
  • Experience with fiber design, OTDR testing, splice management, MPO/MTP systems, and structured-cabling standards.
  • Familiarity with BICSI, TIA/EIA, ISO/IEC, and applicable local codes and safety requirements.
  • Experience with deployment tooling, asset tracking, work-order systems, and dashboard-driven operational management.
  • Relevant certifications such as RCDD, CFOT, PMP, or Lean/Six Sigma.

Success Measures

  • Fiber and low-voltage installation quality and first-pass acceptance rates
  • Reduction in deployment defects, rework, and time to operational handoff
  • Vendor capacity, productivity, and performance

You will collaborate closely with cloud engineers, data engineers, bioinformaticians, AI scientists, computational biologists, and experimental scientists to turn evolving scientific needs into secure, reliable and scalable engineering solutions.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with substantial technical autonomy. You will make cross-system architecture and operational trade-offs, establish reusable engineering patterns, and mentor our Cloud Engineers and Data Engineers through design reviews, delivery and troubleshooting. The role does not require formal line management, but it does require clear technical leadership and accountability for platform outcomes.

This hybrid role is based at the Chesterford Research Campus, near Cambridge, and reports to the Head of Data Infrastructure. The successful candidate will normally work from the campus at least three days per week, participate in operational support and incident escalation, and must have permission to work in the UK.

Responsibilities: 

  • Lead the architecture and evolution of our AWS-based infrastructure across cloud services, scientific data platforms and AI/ML workloads, balancing delivery speed, reliability, security and cost.

Tu seras amené(e) à travailler plus particulièrement sur Vertical Expense, notre solution SaaS de gestion des notes de frais qui accompagne les entreprises et les organisations publiques dans leur transformation digitale. Tu y prendras en charge le développement de grands comptes publics et privés, sur des ventes complexes à forts enjeux. Tu auras pour mission de : Piloter le cycle de vente de bout en bout : qualification des opportunités, proposition de valeur différenciante, accès aux décideurs, négociation et closing. Développer de nouvelles opportunités par une prospection ciblée, en complément des leads apportés par le Marketing et par nos équipes Alliances & Channel. Analyser les besoins de tes prospects et présenter la solution, avec l'appui de l'avant-vente sur les projets complexes. Rédiger les réponses aux appels d'offres publics et privés (dont le mémoire technique), en t'appuyant sur les équipes internes. Assurer une passation fluide vers les équipes projets et CSM, et suivre les projets en appui après la signature. Participer aux réflexions stratégiques : veille concurrentielle, tendances du marché, différenciateurs produit. Ce qu'on va attendre de toi : Tu as une expérience significative et récente en vente complexe SaaS B2B auprès de grands comptes. Tu as déjà mené des cycles de vente longs, dans des organisations multi-décideurs, en travaillant avec des partenaires et des influenceurs. Tu as un vrai goût pour la chasse : aller chercher de nouveaux clients te motive. Tu es à l'aise face à des interlocuteurs C-level et tu sais adapter ton discours à chacun (idéalement DAF, DRH, Travel Manager, DSI…). Tu sais répondre à un appel d'offres avec rigueur, de la réponse au mémoire technique. Tu comprends les solutions SaaS, web et mobiles. Tu es autonome, organisé(e) et tenace, et tu sais rebondir face à un deal perdu. Tu aimes travailler en équipe avec le Marketing, l’équipe Alliance/Channel, les équipes projets et le Produit. Tu es à l'aise avec des déplacements réguliers chez les clients (environ une fois par semaine). C'est un plus si : Tu connais l'univers des notes de frais ou du voyage d'affaires. Tu parles anglais. Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? Un poste stratégique, au cœur de notre développement sur les grands comptes publics et privés. Pas que de la prospection à froid : une partie des leads vient du Marketing et de nos partenaires. Une vision complète du cycle de vente, jusqu'au suivi du projet client. Une équipe stable, fière de ses grands comptes, avec le sens du service et de l'excellence. Une ambiance où l'on ne se prend pas au sérieux : team building réguliers… Processus de recrutement : Entretien téléphonique RH. Entretien avec le manager. Mise en situation : étude de cas sur un compte client fictif. Entretien final avec la Direction. Localisation : Aix-en-Provence, avec 2 jours par semaine sur site et 3 jours de télétravail. description: About AQEMIA AQEMIA is a drug invention company dedicated to creating entirely new medicines to address major unmet medical needs. At the core of our mission is QEMI, our proprietary molecule-invention platform, which uniquely combines cutting-edge science with advanced technology. Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles. What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing never-before-seen molecules, without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies. Our most advanced preclinical programs are currently in vivo optimization, targeting diseases still waiting for effective treatments, offering our teams the opportunity to work on science that can make a real difference in people’s lives. For more information, visit AQEMIA.com, our WTTJ Page, and our LinkedIn. About our Team AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery. This close collaboration across disciplines is central to our approach, enabling us to tackle complex scientific challenges from first principles and translate cutting-edge ideas into novel therapeutic candidates. At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention. The role AQEMIA's drug discovery programs and AI platform increasingly create value through licensing deals and strategic partnerships with pharma and biotech companies. As our first in-house Legal Counsel, you will lead the legal work on these deals from term sheet to signing. You'll make sure each licensing agreement maximises value creation for Aqemia, protects our IP, and the platform behind every program. Beyond licensing, you will become the trusted legal partner for CEO, founders, leadership and teams across the company, covering IP and patents, operational contracts, data and AI, compliance and corporate matters alongside specialist external counsel. Within a year, you will have shaped how legal works at AQEMIA: issues will be mapped and anticipated, processes will be practical, and leadership will rely on you for well-judged legal advice. Reporting to the Corporate Finance Manager, you’ll have a rare chance to sit at the centre of the deals that bring AI-discovered drug candidates to partners, and to grow well beyond licensing into a broad in-house role. Responsibilities Licensing & partnerships: lead the legal work on licensing and collaboration deals, drafting and negotiating agreements from term sheet to signing. Deal strategy: work with BD, Finance and Leadership to turn commercial goals into contract terms, while protecting AQEMIA's platform and other programs. IP & patents: support IP protection and patent-related decisions with scientific teams and external patent counsel. Operational contracts: draft and negotiate NDAs, MTAs, CRO, vendor, software and data agreements, including contractual questions on data use and AI. Corporate & compliance: adresss GDPR, regulatory, compliance and dispute-related matters with specialist support where needed, and support corporate and fundraising matters in coordination with Finance and external advisors. Legal processes: own templates and approval workflows, highlight key contract obligations and deadlines to relevant teams, and manage external counsel. Qualifications Law degree or equivalent professional legal qualification. 5+ years of legal experience, including time at a law firm in a life sciences practice. In-house experience at a biotech or pharma company is a strong plus. Licensing: hands-on experience drafting and negotiating biotech or pharma licensing agreements yourself, not only coordinating external counsel. Deal knowledge: strong understanding of licensing mechanics and IP ownership in drug discovery (scope, exclusivity, financials, termination). Communication: excellent English drafting and negotiation skills, and you can explain legal points clearly to non-lawyers. Mindset: autonomous, pragmatic and eager to learn legal topics beyond your current expertise. Nice‑to‑Have In-house experience at a biotech, pharma or TechBio company, ideally a startup or lean legal team. Exposure to AI, data or technology platform agreements (data rights, model training, ownership of outputs). Experience building legal processes, templates or contract management from scratch. Business development or commercial experience alongside your legal background. Professional French. Our recruitment process 1 - Hiring Manager’s interview: you’ll meet directly with your future manager (45 mins) 2 - Technical assessment of your skills through a Business Case (60 mins) 3 - Cultural fit interview with our co-founder and COO Emmanuelle (45 mins) 4 - Final interview with our co-founder and CEO Maximilien (45 mins) Why Join Us ? At AQEMIA, we work for a mission: joining us means having your own impact on changing the way drugs are discovered, and helping to shape the direction of our fast-growing company and team. Expanding Drug Discovery Pipeline : Focused on critical therapeutic areas like Oncology, CNS, Immuno-inflammation... with in vivo proof of concept/patent stage programs. Collaborations with top Pharma, including a $140M Sanofi deal. World-Class Interdisciplinary Team : work alongside exceptional talent at the intersection of technology and life sciences. Our teams combine deep expertise in AI, physics-based modeling, biology, and medicinal chemistry to push the boundaries of innovation. DeepTech Recognition: AQEMIA is proud to be part of the French Tech 40 and France 2030, highlighting our role as a key player in Europe’s DeepTech ecosystem. Prime Location with Flexibility : Our offices are located in the heart of Paris and London (King’s Cross), with flexible work arrangements including up to two remote days per week. About Nscale

Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Network Engineer to build and bring up the networks behind Nscale's GPU clusters across Europe. You'll join our Deployment organisation, a build org that owns every step from hardware arrival on site through to customer acceptance.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll take network designs into production: configuring and validating cluster fabrics, front-end networks, and WAN edge, troubleshooting issues during bring-up, and making sure every build is ready for customers. The role involves regular travel to our sites.

What You'll be Doing

  • Deploy, configure, and validate high-performance Ethernet and InfiniBand fabrics for large GPU clusters.
  • Bring up front-end, storage, and management networks and WAN edge connectivity for new sites and expansions.
  • Run network acceptance testing and performance validation ahead of customer handover.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues across routing, switching, optics, and cabling during build and early life.
  • Work with Network Architecture to refine reference designs, BOMs, and build standards based on what you learn in the field.
  • Build and improve automation for provisioning, configuration, and validation.
  • Partner with Technical Program Managers, Data Centre Operations, and vendors to keep builds on schedule.
  • Write clear runbooks and documentation so builds are repeatable across sites.

About You

  • 5+ years of network engineering experience in large-scale data centre, cloud, or HPC environments.
  • Experience at a hyperscaler or major network vendor (e.g. Microsoft, AWS, Oracle/OCI, Cisco) or a comparable large-scale network.
  • Strong hands-on knowledge of routing and switching: BGP, OSPF, EVPN/VXLAN, ECMP, and L2/L3 data centre design.
  • Experience deploying and operating cluster networks, ideally including InfiniBand or RoCE fabrics.
  • Practical experience with network automation (Python, Ansible, or similar).
  • Calm, methodical troubleshooter who can work under deadline pressure on live builds.
  • Willingness to travel across Europe to sites as needed.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building networks for GPU clusters or AI training environments.
  • Familiarity with HPC topologies (Fat Tree, Rail) and 400G/800G optics.
  • Experience with SONiC, Cumulus, or other open networking platforms.
  • WAN, peering, or DWDM experience.
  • Industry certifications such as CCNP/CCIE, JNCIP/JNCIE, or NVIDIA networking certifications.

Why this role matters

The network is what turns thousands of GPUs into a single system. Your work decides how fast new clusters reach customers and how well they perform once they do.

We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities. We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.
